items.title: Vince Giordano interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 11, 2007
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] I’ve heard variations on that story. That’s so funny. Derek Smith, the piano player, they took him in a room and they said, “what is that?” ... [INTERVIEWEE] Exactly. Oh it was some wild times.

ctx.x: No. No. They would come over and — “don’t play that stuff, don’t play that stuff.” They couldn’t understand me for anything. That’s fine. I chose the other path as the poet said. The one fateful day that really got me thinking about pursuing a career in this music was I was playing one of my old recordings and I had my tuba home, and I listened to it and I decided to try to play along with the recording. And I was maybe 12 years old. I could feel the beat but I really didn’t have enough musicality to understand…

I’ve heard variations on that story. That’s so funny. Derek Smith, the piano player, they took him in a room and they said, “what is that?” He said, “what do you mean?” He says, “what is that?” He says, “it’s a piano.” He says, “you’re in.”
Exactly. Oh it was some wild times.
